items.label: Industry: Search, Digital Advertising & Cloud/AI Infrastructure
items.detail: Selected from active-conviction account holdings: GOOG (Alphabet, 6 sh, $2,012.28, 0.42% of NAV) shares the account's entire Telecomm/Communication-Services sleeve with TTWO (3.93% of NAV combined) but has never itself been the anchor of a dedicated scout cycle -- the 2026-09-06 cycle was grounded in TTWO and covered gaming, mentioning GOOG only in passing as the sleeve-mate. Search/ads/cloud is also a live, fast-moving theme this cycle: Google's Q2 2026 remedies judgment in the DOJ search-monopoly case took effect February 2026 (no Chrome divestiture, but both sides are now cross-appealing at the D.C. Circuit), Google Cloud revenue grew 63% YoY to $20B on a $462B backlog, and Gemini 3 / AI Mode has become a real two-sided story for the core Search business -- a genuine growth driver but also the source of real disintermediation risk from AI-native answer engines.

items.label: GOOG
items.detail: Existing holding, thesis reinforced with real new evidence: Google Cloud revenue hit $20B in the most recent quarter (+63% YoY, a $462B backlog), and Gemini 3.1 Pro / AI Mode integration pushed overall Search query volume to an all-time high even as queries get longer and more complex -- core AI-response cost is down >30% and latency down 35% over five years, evidence Alphabet can absorb the compute cost of AI answers without destroying Search's economics. Ad-side monetization is following: Performance Max now captures over 30% of customer search ad spend, and Gemini-driven ad-relevance improvements are running near +10%. The DOJ search-monopoly remedies that took effect February 2026 were narrower than feared (no Chrome divestiture, no ban on default-search payments to Apple), though the DOJ/states have cross-appealed for the harsher structural relief the trial court declined to order, keeping a real tail risk alive at the D.C. Circuit into 2027. Genuine, unresolved risk: AI Overviews cause a 61% click-through-rate drop on the queries where they appear, and independent AI-first answer engines (ChatGPT Search >1B MAU, Perplexity ~45M MAU, 7.67% share of AI-chatbot referral traffic vs. Google's own Gemini app at 7.03%) are pulling a real, if still small relative to Google's ~80% of global query volume, slice of informational search away from the traditional ad-supported results page.
items.diversification_note: GOOG is already paired with TTWO as the account's entire Telecomm/Communication-Services sleeve (3.93% of NAV, $19,059) -- reinforcing here deepens an existing sleeve rather than diversifying it, and any new AI-infrastructure names below would additionally overlap with the account's existing CRWV/GEV AI-datacenter-power holdings (2.76%/1.97% of NAV).

items.label: AVGO
items.detail: Broadcom -- not currently held. Functions as picks-and-shovels infrastructure for the custom-silicon side of the AI/cloud buildout rather than betting on any single hyperscaler's ad or cloud business: Broadcom is the co-design partner behind Google's TPU program (long-term supply agreement through 2031) and has parallel custom-accelerator deals with Meta (>1 GW, extended through 2029), OpenAI (10 GW, first deployments 2H 2026), and Anthropic (3.5 GW of TPU-linked capacity) -- diversified across all the major AI capex spenders rather than dependent on Google alone. AI semiconductor revenue hit $8.4B in the most recent quarter (+106% YoY), with a disclosed $73B AI backlog and management guidance for >$100B of AI-chip revenue in 2027. Last price $361.73 (+0.25% on the day). Real risk: this thesis is a bet on the whole hyperscaler AI-capex cycle continuing at its current pace -- a broad slowdown in AI infrastructure spending (by Google or any of Broadcom's other big customers) would hit this name harder than a single-hyperscaler-specific holding.
items.suggested_size: Small-to-modest starter, roughly 0.5-1% of account NAV (~$2,400-$4,800), sized down given it would sit alongside the account's existing CRWV/GEV AI-infrastructure exposure rather than diversify away from it.

items.label: TTD
items.detail: The Trade Desk -- not currently held. An independent, non-walled-garden alternative to GOOG's ad stack (100% demand-side-platform revenue, no owned media inventory, so structurally free of the conflict-of-interest Alphabet/Amazon face selling into their own inventory) -- a real business-model differentiation, not just a smaller comp. But the fundamentals are genuinely deteriorating, not a clean value story yet: the stock lost roughly 52% of its value in H1 2026 as Amazon's aggressive DSP entry (Amazon ad revenue +23% YoY in Q4 2025 vs. TTD's decelerating growth) forced visible fee/growth compression -- 2025 revenue growth slowed to 18% from 26% in 2024, and Q2 2026 revenue grew just 3% YoY to $715M, a sharp miss on what had been 25%+ growth as recently as Q1 2025. Last price $14.30 (+2.36% on the day, well off prior highs). Flagging as a watch item rather than a new position: the post-crash valuation reset is real, but Amazon's ability to subsidize ad-tech pricing with e-commerce/cloud profits is a structural threat to TTD's take rate that has not yet stabilized -- worth revisiting once growth deceleration shows signs of bottoming.

items.label: AI answer engines / agentic search disintermediation
items.detail: No specific new ticker (Perplexity and OpenAI's ChatGPT are private), theme-level signal: ChatGPT Search crossed 1B monthly active users in May 2026 and Perplexity has grown to ~45M MAU on a $20B valuation, abandoning ads entirely in February 2026 to chase $500M of annualized subscription revenue instead -- a genuinely different monetization model than Google's ad-supported results page. Statcounter's May 2026 AI-chatbot referral data puts Perplexity at 7.67% share, narrowly ahead of Google's own Gemini app at 7.03%, and Google's AI Overviews already cut click-through to underlying web results by 61% on the queries where they appear. Google still carries roughly 80% of global query volume, so this is not yet an existential threat, but the disruption is concentrated exactly in the informational/research queries that used to drive organic traffic and ad clicks -- carry forward to the next scout cycle to track whether Google's own AI Mode successfully recaptures this traffic or cedes it to standalone answer engines.

items.label: Google search-antitrust remedies appeal (D.C. Circuit)
items.detail: No specific ticker beyond GOOG itself, theme-level regulatory signal: the December 2025 final remedies judgment in the DOJ's search-monopoly case was narrower than the government sought (no Chrome divestiture, no ban on default-search payments to Apple/others; only data-sharing/search-syndication requirements for qualified competitors, which took effect February 2026 while the underlying systems are still being built). Google filed its own appeal (D.C. Circuit No. 26-5023) challenging both liability and remedies, and the DOJ plus a coalition of states cross-appealed pressing for the harsher structural relief (Chrome divestiture, ending the Apple default-search deal) that the trial court declined to order. Briefing continued through summer 2026 with no schedule yet for oral argument, meaning the appeal is likely to run well into 2027 -- a real, live tail risk on the Search/ads moat that is not resolved by the current remedies already in effect, worth tracking rather than acting on until the D.C. Circuit rules.
